## Consistencia: convergencia visual en R

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 4.4
#| fig-align: center
set.seed(42)
pop <- rexp(500000, rate = 1/5.2)  # rendimiento exponencial, media=5.2
ns  <- seq(5, 300, by = 5)
medias <- sapply(ns, function(n) mean(sample(pop, n)))

par(mar = c(4.5, 4.5, 3, 1), family = "sans")
plot(ns, medias, type = "l", col = "#1e3a8a", lwd = 1.5,
     xlab = "Tamaño de muestra n",
     ylab = expression(bar(x)),
     main = "Convergencia del estimador: la media muestral converge a μ = 5.2 ton/ha",
     cex.main = 1.15, ylim = c(3.5, 7.5), cex.lab = 1.1)
abline(h = mean(pop), col = "#15803d", lwd = 2.5, lty = 2)
abline(h = mean(pop) + c(-1,1)*1.96*sd(pop)/sqrt(ns),
       col = "#f59e0b", lwd = 1, lty = 3)
polygon(c(ns, rev(ns)),
        c(mean(pop) + 1.96*sd(pop)/sqrt(ns),
          rev(mean(pop) - 1.96*sd(pop)/sqrt(ns))),
        col = adjustcolor("#bfdbfe", 0.3), border = NA)
text(280, mean(pop)+0.15, expression(mu == 5.2),
     col = "#15803d", cex = 1.1, font = 2)
legend("topright", legend = c("Media muestral", "μ real", "IC 95%"),
       col = c("#1e3a8a","#15803d","#f59e0b"),
       lwd = c(1.5,2.5,1), lty = c(1,2,3), bty = "n", cex = 1)
box(col = "gray40")
```

<div class="block-note fragment fade-up" data-fragment-index="1" style="margin-top: 8px;">
<div class="block-body" style="font-size: 25px; text-align: center;">
La variabilidad de $\bar{x}$ disminuye con $n$ (consistencia). La banda azul (IC 95%) se estrecha en forma de $1/\sqrt{n}$: necesitamos cuadruplicar $n$ para reducir la incertidumbre a la mitad.
</div>
</div>
